name: active_alerts
title: Active alerts
description: Alerts in LibreNMS, grouped by device, with rule name, severity and age. With no time window: the alerts open now (firing or acknowledged), worst first, for "what's alerting?" or "is anything critical?". On LibreNMS 26.10 and later one alert is a rule firing on a device, and may hold several faults - one per core, port or sensor it matched: fault_count says how many, faults lists them, and totals counts alerts and faults separately. alert_id is the first fault's ID, for alert_details; group_id names the device and rule. With a window (hours, or since/until): every alert raised in it, including ones that have since recovered, each with still_open and recovered_at - for "what fired overnight?" or "what alerted between Friday and Monday?". The window is either hours (1 to 168, counting back from until) or since/until. Each of since and until is a duration before now (90m, 24h, 7d) or an ISO 8601 time; until defaults to now, and the window defaults to the last 24 hours. Filter by severity, device, device group or location. Paged: 50 by default, up to 100; use page.next_offset for more. Records are short unless verbose is true.

severity.description: Only alerts of this severity: critical, warning or ok. Leave out for all.

device.description: Only alerts on this device: hostname, display name, IP address or LibreNMS device ID. Leave out for every device.

group.description: Only devices in this LibreNMS device group (by name; list_groups_and_locations shows them).

location.description: Only devices at this location (by name; list_groups_and_locations shows them).

hours.description: Alerts raised in the last this many hours, 1 to 168. Leave out for alerts open now.

since.description: Alerts raised since: a duration before now (90m, 24h, 7d) or an ISO 8601 time. Leave out for alerts open now.

until.description: Alerts raised until: a duration before now or an ISO 8601 time. Defaults to now.

offset.description: How many alerts to skip, for paging. Start at 0, then use page.next_offset.

limit.description: How many alerts to return, 1 to 100. Defaults to 50.

verbose.description: Include each alert's start time and note.

name: alert_details
title: Alert details
description: Everything about one alert: why it fired (the ports, sensors or other things the rule matched, with the values that tripped it), the rule's name, severity, condition, procedure link and notes, its state, acknowledgement note and how long it's been open, and how often the same rule has fired on the same device in the last 30 days, with the most recent times - to tell a one-off from a flapping alert. Takes an alert ID, which active_alerts gives for open alerts. On LibreNMS 26.10 and later that's a fault ID: the details are that fault's own (never another core's or port's), and group lists every fault the same rule has open on the device.

alert_id.description: The LibreNMS alert ID - on 26.10 and later, a fault ID - from active_alerts (alert_id, or a fault_id from its faults).

name: alert_rules
title: Alert rules
description: LibreNMS's alert rules: each one's name, severity, whether it's enabled, its condition, which devices, device groups and locations it applies to (or all), its alert template, how many alerts it has open now and how many it raised in the last 7 days. For "what are we alerting on?", "why didn't X alert?" or "which rules are noisiest?". Filter by part of the name or by severity; sort by name, open or raised. On LibreNMS 26.10 and later each rule also says whether it notifies per entity (notify_per_entity, max_entities - null max_entities inherits the server's default, 20 unless changed), which decides whether acknowledging one fault acknowledges the device's others, and flags conditions using device columns 26.10 removed (removed_columns; latency is now device_stats.ping_rtt_last). Paged: 50 by default, up to 100. Read-only: rules can only be changed in LibreNMS.

name.description: Only rules whose name contains this.

severity.description: Only rules of this severity: critical, warning or ok.

include_disabled.description: Include disabled rules (by default only enabled ones are listed).

sort.description: Sort by name (the default), open (most open alerts first) or raised (most raised in the last 7 days first).

offset.description: How many rules to skip, for paging. Start at 0, then use page.next_offset.

limit.description: How many rules to return, 1 to 100. Defaults to 50.

verbose.description: Include each rule's notes and procedure link.

name: config_backup
title: Config backup
description: A device's configuration as Unimus backed it up: the newest backup by default, or an earlier one by ID, with the list of recent backups (each is a config version: valid_since is when Unimus first saw it, valid_until when it last confirmed it unchanged). For "what's configured on X?", "is VLAN 120 on this switch?" or reading an old version. Secrets (passwords, keys, SNMP communities, private keys) are redacted. If the server is set to MCP_CONFIG_TEXT=summary, only sizes, times and line counts come back, never config text. Long configs are paged by line: 200 lines by default, up to 1000; use lines.next_offset for more. To compare versions, use config_diff.

device.description: The device: hostname, display name, IP address or LibreNMS device ID.

backup_id.description: A backup ID from the backups list. Leave out for the newest.

offset.description: How many lines to skip, for paging. Start at 0, then use lines.next_offset.

limit.description: How many lines to return, 1 to 1000. Defaults to 200.

name: config_diff
title: Config diff
description: The difference between two of a device's Unimus config backups, as changed lines only (- removed, + added). By default the newest backup against the one before it; give from_backup and to_backup (IDs from config_backup's list) for any two. Secrets (passwords, keys, SNMP communities, private keys) are redacted. If the server is set to MCP_CONFIG_TEXT=summary, only sizes, times and line counts come back, never config text. Long diffs are cut at 200 lines, with the total counted. For changes in a time window together with events and logs, use what_changed.

device.description: The device: hostname, display name, IP address or LibreNMS device ID.

from_backup.description: The older backup's ID. Leave out (with to_backup) for the one before the newest.

to_backup.description: The newer backup's ID. Leave out for the newest.

name: device_details
title: Device details
description: One device's details beyond its health, in sections - ask only for the ones the question needs: inventory (chassis, modules, transceivers, power supplies, fans with models and serials); vlans (each VLAN with its untagged and tagged ports); fdb (MAC addresses learned per port - "what's connected to port X?"); arp (IP to MAC entries); poe (PoE power budget used and left); wireless (access points, clients, channel and signal sensors); routing (BGP sessions, OSPF neighbours, VRFs); availability (uptime percentage over the last day, week, month and year); addresses (the device's own IP addresses and which port each is on). Without sections, everything except fdb and arp. Lists are paged together with offset and limit (50 rows by default, up to 200); a section that couldn't be read is listed under unavailable. For health, use device_health; for sensors, device_sensors; for neighbours, device_neighbours.

device.description: The device: hostname, display name, IP address or LibreNMS device ID.

sections.description: Which sections to return: any of inventory, vlans, fdb, arp, poe, wireless, routing, availability, addresses. Leave out for all but fdb and arp.

offset.description: How many rows to skip in each list, for paging. Start at 0, then use the next_offset a section's page gives.

limit.description: How many rows to return per list, 1 to 200. Defaults to 50.

name: device_events
title: Device events
description: A device's history from LibreNMS for a window of time, newest first: event log entries (interface changes, reboots, discovery), alert state changes, and outages with their length. Use it for "what happened to X?", "when did X go down?" or "what happened between 2 and 4 last night?". The window is either hours (1 to 168, counting back from until) or since/until. Each of since and until is a duration before now (90m, 24h, 7d) or an ISO 8601 time; until defaults to now, and the window defaults to the last 24 hours. Paged: 50 entries by default; pass the next_offset from page for more. If LibreNMS's logs don't reach back to the window's start, window_complete is false and covered_since says how far they did reach. Config changes and syslog aren't included; what_changed adds those.

device.description: The device: hostname, display name, IP address or LibreNMS device ID.

hours.description: How many hours to look back from until, 1 to 168. Leave out when using since.

since.description: Start of the window: a duration before now (90m, 24h, 7d) or an ISO 8601 time.

until.description: End of the window: a duration before now or an ISO 8601 time. Defaults to now.

offset.description: How many entries to skip, for paging. Start at 0, then use page.next_offset.

limit.description: How many entries to return, 1 to 100. Defaults to 50.

name: device_health
title: Device health
description: How one device is doing now: up or down, uptime, whether it's in a maintenance window, its open alerts, peak CPU, memory and fullest storage, and the ports that are down while enabled or are counting errors (top 5). Use it for "is X OK?" questions. It doesn't cover history; use device_events or what_changed for that, and port_status for one port in detail.

device.description: The device: hostname, display name, IP address or LibreNMS device ID.

name: device_neighbours
title: Device neighbours
description: Every LLDP and CDP neighbour of one device: the local port, the device on the other end (with its LibreNMS ID when LibreNMS knows it), its port, platform and protocol. Includes neighbours that report this device but that it doesn't report itself (seen_from: neighbour), which often means a discovery problem on one side. Use it for "what's connected to this switch?" or topology questions. For one port, port_status shows its neighbour too.

device.description: The device: hostname, display name, IP address or LibreNMS device ID.

name: device_sensors
title: Device sensors
description: One device's sensor readings: temperatures, fan speeds, optical power in dBm, signal, voltages, currents, power and more. Each reading has its unit, its limits and a state (ok, warning, critical, or unknown when there's nothing to judge it by), judged the way DashyNMS's Health tab judges it: the sensor's own LibreNMS limits where it has them, sensible defaults for dBm, signal, temperature and fans where it doesn't. Problems first. Types are LibreNMS's sensor classes - temperature, fanspeed, dbm (optical power), signal, voltage, current, power, humidity and others - and fan, optics and temp work too. For the same across the whole network, use health_overview.

device.description: The device: hostname, display name, IP address or LibreNMS device ID.

type.description: Only this type of sensor, e.g. temperature, fanspeed, dbm or voltage. Leave out for all.

name: find_device
title: Find a device
description: Search LibreNMS for devices by part of a hostname, display name or sysName, by IP address, or by MAC address, and/or list devices by status, device group or location. Use it when the exact device isn't known yet, to get device IDs for the other tools, or for "which devices are down at site X?". A MAC address is looked up in LibreNMS's ARP tables, so it finds the routers or layer-3 switches that have seen it (with the IP it had), not the endpoint itself. Best matches first. Paged: 10 by default, up to 50; when page.next_offset is set, call again with that offset to get every match rather than making narrower searches. Records are short unless verbose is true. It doesn't show health or alerts.

query.description: Part of a hostname, display name or sysName, an IP address, or a MAC address (any common format). Can be left out when status, group or location is given.

status.description: Only devices with this status: up, down or disabled.

group.description: Only devices in this LibreNMS device group (by name; list_groups_and_locations shows them).

location.description: Only devices at this location (by name; list_groups_and_locations shows them).

offset.description: How many matches to skip, for paging. Start at 0, then use page.next_offset.

limit.description: How many matches to return, 1 to 50. Defaults to 10.

verbose.description: Return every field (sysName, OS, hardware, last polled) instead of the short record.

name: graph
title: Graph
description: A LibreNMS graph as an image, shown in the chat: a device's graph (traffic, processor, memory, ping, temperature and the rest of its health graphs) or one port's (traffic, packets, errors). Use it when a picture of a trend helps: "show me the traffic on X this week". Without type, a device gives its traffic graph and the list of graph types it has; a port gives its traffic. With sensor, one sensor alone on its own scale (one temperature, one optic's power) rather than every sensor of its kind together; device_sensors lists them with their IDs. The time range is range (hour, day, week, month or year; a day by default), or since and until for a custom span up to 31 days. The legend lists every line with its figures; turn it off (legend: false) for graphs with many lines, where it would dwarf the graph. The image has its own white background with dark text: show it as it is, on a light background, and never recolour it or place it on a dark one, where it can't be read. For numbers rather than a picture, use port_status, device_health or device_sensors.

device.description: The device: hostname, display name, IP address or LibreNMS device ID.

type.description: The graph type. For a device: a name from its list (device_bits, device_processor, device_mempool, device_icmp_perf, ...) or traffic, cpu, memory, ping, temperature, storage. For a port: bits (traffic), upkts, nupkts or errors. Leave out for traffic.

port.description: A port on the device, for that port's graph: its name (ifName), description, alias or port ID. Leave out for a device graph.

sensor.description: One sensor on the device, for that sensor's own graph: its sensor_id from device_sensors, or its description (e.g. "Chassis Temperature"). Type, if given, narrows it to that kind of sensor. Leave out for a device or port graph.

range.description: How far back: hour, day, week, month or year. Defaults to day. Ignored when since is given.

since.description: Start of a custom span: relative ("6h", "3d") or ISO 8601 (UTC unless a zone is given). Up to 31 days before until.

until.description: End of a custom span, the same forms as since. Defaults to now.

legend.description: Draw the legend under the graph (each line's current, average and maximum). Defaults to true. Turn it off for a graph with many lines - a processor graph with a line per core, a device's traffic across dozens of ports - where the legend would be taller than the graph; keep it when the figures matter to the question.

name: health_overview
title: Health overview
description: Sensor readings across the whole network, worst first, for questions like "is anything running hot?", "which optics are low?" or "any fans failing?". By default only readings in warning or critical; set only_problems to false for every reading of a type. Judged the same way as device_sensors. Types are LibreNMS's sensor classes - temperature, fanspeed, dbm (optical power), signal, voltage, current, power, humidity and others - and fan, optics and temp work too. Filter by device group or location. Paged: 50 by default, up to 100.

type.description: Only this type of sensor, e.g. temperature, fanspeed, dbm or voltage. Leave out for every type.

only_problems.description: Only readings in warning or critical (the default). False lists every reading, which needs a type.

group.description: Only devices in this LibreNMS device group (by name; list_groups_and_locations shows them).

location.description: Only devices at this location (by name; list_groups_and_locations shows them).

offset.description: How many readings to skip, for paging. Start at 0, then use page.next_offset.

limit.description: How many readings to return, 1 to 100. Defaults to 50.

name: list_groups_and_locations
title: Device groups and locations
description: The device groups defined in LibreNMS and the locations devices are at, with how many devices are at each location and how many of those are down. Use it to find the names the group and location filters of find_device and active_alerts accept, or for "which sites are there?". To list a group's devices, call find_device with that group.

name: network_events
title: Network events
description: The event log and/or alert log for the whole network over a window of time, newest first, as desktop's Logs tab - for "what happened overnight?" or "anything rebooted today?". The event log has interface changes, reboots, discovery and user actions; the alert log has every alert state change. The window is either hours (1 to 168, counting back from until) or since/until. Each of since and until is a duration before now (90m, 24h, 7d) or an ISO 8601 time; until defaults to now, and the window defaults to the last 24 hours. Filter by event type, severity, device, device group or location. Paged: 50 by default, up to 100. If LibreNMS's logs don't reach back to the window's start, window_complete is false. For one device, device_events also adds its outages.

log.description: Which log: events (the default), alerts, or both.

hours.description: How many hours to look back from until, 1 to 168. Leave out when using since.

since.description: Start of the window: a duration before now (90m, 24h, 7d) or an ISO 8601 time.

until.description: End of the window: a duration before now or an ISO 8601 time. Defaults to now.

type.description: Only event-log entries of this type, e.g. interface, reboot, discovery, system. Part of the type is enough.

severity.description: Only event-log entries of this severity or worse: ok, info, notice, warning or critical.

device.description: Only this device: hostname, display name, IP address or LibreNMS device ID.

group.description: Only devices in this LibreNMS device group (by name).

location.description: Only devices at this location (by name).

offset.description: How many entries to skip, for paging. Start at 0, then use page.next_offset.

limit.description: How many entries to return, 1 to 100. Defaults to 50.

name: network_overview
title: Network overview
description: The whole network in one call, as the dashboard's counts: how many devices are up, down, disabled or ignored, which locations have the most devices down, open alerts by severity and how many are acknowledged, how many ports are down while enabled or counting errors, and the LibreNMS version. A cheap first call for "how's the network?" before drilling in with find_device, active_alerts or the top_ tools.

name: port_status
title: Port status
description: One port on one device: admin and operational state, speed, duplex, VLAN, current traffic and error rates, its description (alias), and the neighbour LibreNMS sees on it (LLDP/CDP). Use it for "is port X up?" or "what's plugged into X?". Rates are LibreNMS's last polling interval, not history. For every problem port on a device at once, use device_health.

device.description: The device: hostname, display name, IP address or LibreNMS device ID.

port.description: The port: its name (ifName, e.g. 1/1/7 or Gi0/1), description (ifDescr), alias, or LibreNMS port ID.

name: recent_config_changes
title: Recent config changes
description: Every device whose configuration changed in a window of time, according to Unimus, newest change first - for "what changed in the network since Friday?" or "has anyone touched the core switches today?". The window is either hours (1 to 168, counting back from until) or since/until. Each of since and until is a duration before now (90m, 24h, 7d) or an ISO 8601 time; until defaults to now, and the window defaults to the last 24 hours. Filter by device group or location (much quicker on a big network: each device is one request to Unimus). Devices Unimus backs up but LibreNMS doesn't know are included when there's no filter. This says when each device changed; config_diff on a device shows what changed. Paged: 50 by default, up to 100.

hours.description: How many hours to look back from until, 1 to 168. Leave out when using since.

since.description: Start of the window: a duration before now (90m, 24h, 7d) or an ISO 8601 time.

until.description: End of the window: a duration before now or an ISO 8601 time. Defaults to now.

group.description: Only devices in this LibreNMS device group (by name).

location.description: Only devices at this location (by name).

offset.description: How many changes to skip, for paging. Start at 0, then use page.next_offset.

limit.description: How many changes to return, 1 to 100. Defaults to 50.

name: search_logs
title: Search logs
description: Searches Graylog's log messages across the network or for one device, over any window up to 31 days: "any errors from the core switches overnight?", "what did this firewall log between 2 and 4am?". Gives the message count first, then the busiest sources, levels, facilities and applications, messages over time, and the newest lines. Narrow it by text in the message, a device (matched on its names and addresses, as LibreNMS's Graylog tab does), a maximum syslog level (0 emergency to 7 debug: 3 means errors and worse) and a stream. The count and messages over time are exact for any window; the busiest values and the lines come from up to 150 messages, and top_from says which. When nothing matches, it says what might be why. For a device's logs alongside its events and config changes, use what_changed.

text.description: Words to find in the message text, matched as a phrase. Leave out for every message.

device.description: A device whose messages to search: hostname, display name, IP address or LibreNMS device ID. Leave out for the whole network.

since.description: Start of the window: relative ("90m", "6h", "3d") or ISO 8601 (UTC unless a zone is given). Defaults to 24 hours before until.

until.description: End of the window, the same forms as since. Defaults to now.

hours.description: Shorthand for since: this many hours before until, 1 to 168. Use since instead for longer windows.

level.description: Only messages at this syslog level or more severe: 0 emergency, 1 alert, 2 critical, 3 error, 4 warning, 5 notice, 6 informational, 7 debug.

stream.description: A Graylog stream, by title or ID. Leave out for every stream the account can read.

limit.description: How many of the newest lines to return, 0 to 50. Defaults to 20; 0 for the counts alone.

name: top_devices
title: Top devices
description: The devices that stand out across the network: by traffic (the default, all their ports' traffic summed, as desktop's Top devices widget) or by problems (most ports down while enabled or counting errors). Filter by device group or location.

by.description: Rank by traffic (the default), in, out, or problems.

limit.description: How many devices, 1 to 50. Defaults to 10.

group.description: Only devices in this LibreNMS device group (by name).

location.description: Only devices at this location (by name).

name: top_errors
title: Top errors
description: The ports counting the most errors across the network right now, in errors per second in and out, by LibreNMS's last polling interval. An empty list means no port is counting errors. Rank by total, in or out; filter by device group or location. As desktop's Top errors widget.

by.description: Rank by total (the default), in or out.

limit.description: How many ports, 1 to 50. Defaults to 10.

group.description: Only devices in this LibreNMS device group (by name).

location.description: Only devices at this location (by name).

name: top_interfaces
title: Top interfaces
description: The busiest ports across the network right now, by LibreNMS's last polling interval: traffic in and out in Mbps and as a share of the port's speed. Rank by total, in or out. Filter by device group or location. As desktop's Top interfaces widget. For traffic history, use the device's graphs.

by.description: Rank by total (the default), in or out.

limit.description: How many ports, 1 to 50. Defaults to 10.

group.description: Only devices in this LibreNMS device group (by name).

location.description: Only devices at this location (by name).

name: trace_endpoint
title: Trace endpoint
description: Finds where a MAC or IPv4 address is plugged in: the switch and edge port, with its alias, VLAN and state. An IP is turned into its MAC through LibreNMS's ARP tables, then every switch whose forwarding table has learned the MAC is checked, and ports that are links to other switches (LLDP/CDP neighbours, aggregates, ports with many MACs) are passed over. Also gives every port the MAC was seen on, with its role, and the path of switches from the edge upwards. Says when the answer is ambiguous - several possible edge ports, or only uplinks - rather than guessing. Only as current as LibreNMS's last FDB and ARP poll.

address.description: A MAC address (any common form: aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff, aabb.ccdd.eeff, AA-BB-...) or an IPv4 address.

name: what_changed
title: What changed
description: Everything that changed on a device in a window of time, from every source configured: the LibreNMS timeline (as device_events, up to 30 entries), the config diff for the newest Unimus backup that began inside the window, against the one before it (secrets redacted, long diffs cut), and how many Graylog messages it sent, with up to 10 of the newest. Use it when something broke and the question is why. The window is either hours (1 to 168, counting back from until) or since/until. Each of since and until is a duration before now (90m, 24h, 7d) or an ISO 8601 time; until defaults to now, and the window defaults to the last 24 hours. Graylog is only counted for windows that end now. Each source says when it isn't configured or couldn't be reached.

device.description: The device: hostname, display name, IP address or LibreNMS device ID.

hours.description: How many hours to look back from until, 1 to 168. Leave out when using since.

since.description: Start of the window: a duration before now (90m, 24h, 7d) or an ISO 8601 time.

until.description: End of the window: a duration before now or an ISO 8601 time. Defaults to now.
